readings.title: The Potter's Shattered Jug
readings.subtitle: A Prophecy in the Valley of Hinnom
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 19:1] Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“Go and get a potter’s earthen jug, and take some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests.</dq>
[2] <dq>“Then you shall go out to the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, which is by the entry of the Potsherd Gate, and shall proclaim there <dn>את</dn> the words that <dn>I</dn> speak to you,</dq>
[3] <dq>and shall say, ‘Hear the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, O sovereigns of Yehuḏah and inhabitants of Yerushalayim. Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, “See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing evil on this place, that makes the ears tingle of all who hear it.</dq>
[4] <dq>“Because they have forsaken <dn>את</dn> <dn>Me</dn> and have profaned <dn>את</dn> this place, and have burned incense in it to other mighty ones whom neither they, their fathers, nor the sovereigns of Yehuḏah have known, and they have filled this place with the blood of the innocents,</dq>
[5] <dq>and have built <dn>את</dn> the high places of Ba‛al, to burn their sons with fire for ascending offerings to Ba‛al, which <dn>I</dn> did not command or speak, nor did it come into <dn>My</dn> heart.</dq>
[6] <dq>“Therefore see, the days are coming,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“that this place shall no more be called Topheth or the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, but rather the Valley of Slaughter.</dq>
[7] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall pour out <dn>את</dn> the counsel of Yehuḏah and Yerushalayim in this place, and <dn>I</dn> shall make them fall by the sword before their enemies and by the hands of those who seek their lives. And <dn>I</dn> shall give their corpses as meat for the birds of the heavens and for the beasts of the earth.</dq>
[8] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make <dn>את</dn> this city a ruin, and a hissing – everyone who passes by it is appalled and hisses because of all its plagues.</dq>
[9] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make them to eat <dn>את</dn> the flesh of their sons and <dn>את</dn> the flesh of their daughters, and eat one another’s flesh in the siege and in the distress with which their enemies and those who seek their lives distress them.” ’</dq>

readings.title: The Potter's Shattered Jug
readings.subtitle: The Unrepairable Nation
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 19:10] <dq>“And you shall break the jug before the eyes of the men who go with you,</dq>
[11] <dq>and shall say to them, ‘Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, “Even so <dn>I</dn> break <dn>את</dn> this people and <dn>את</dn> this city, as one breaks a potter’s vessel, which one is unable to repair again. And let them bury them in Topheth till there is no place to bury.</dq>
[12] <dq>“This is what <dn>I</dn> shall do to this place,”</dq> declares <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>“and to its inhabitants, so as to make this city like Topheth.</dq>
[13] <dq>“And the houses of Yerushalayim and the houses of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah shall be as unclean as the place of Topheth, because of all the houses on whose roofs they have burned incense to all the host of the heavens, and poured out drink offerings to other mighty ones.” ’ ”</dq>
[14] And when Yirmeyahu returned from Topheth, where <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> had sent him to prophesy, he stood in the courtyard of the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> and said to all the people,
[15] “Thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, the <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am bringing on this city and on all her towns <dn>את</dn> all the evil that <dn>I</dn> have pronounced against it, because they have stiffened their necks so as not to hear <dn>My</dn> words.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Pashhur's Opposition
readings.subtitle: Jeremiah is Beaten and Put in Stocks
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 20:1] And Pashḥur son of Imměr, the priest who was also chief governor in the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, heard that Yirmeyahu prophesied <dn>את</dn> these words,
[2] And Pashḥur struck <dn>את</dn> Yirmeyahu the prophet, and put <dn>את</dn> him in the stocks that were in the high gate of Binyamin, which was by the House of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.
[3] And it came to be on the next day that Pashḥur brought Yirmeyahu out of the stocks, and Yirmeyahu said to him, “<dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has not called your name Pashḥur, but Maḡor-Missaḇiḇ.
[4] “For thus said <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, <dq>‘See, <dn>I</dn> am making you a fear to yourself and to all your loved ones. And they shall fall by the sword of their enemies, while your eyes see it. And <dn>I</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> all Yehuḏah into the hand of the sovereign of Baḇel, and he shall exile them to Baḇel and strike them with the sword.</dq>
[5] <dq>And <dn>I</dn> shall give <dn>את</dn> all the wealth of this city and <dn>את</dn> all its labour, and <dn>את</dn> all its valuables, and <dn>את</dn> all the treasures of the sovereigns of Yehuḏah, <dn>I</dn> give into the hand of their enemies, who shall plunder them, seize them, and shall bring them to Baḇel.</dq>
[6] <dq>And you, Pashḥur, and all who dwell in your house, shall go into captivity, and enter into Baḇel. And there you shall die, and be buried there, you and all your loved ones, to whom you have prophesied falsehood.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: Jeremiah's Lament
readings.subtitle: The Unquenchable Word and Unwavering Trust
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 20:7] O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, You enticed me, and <dn>I</dn> was enticed. You are stronger than <dn>I</dn>, and have prevailed. <dn>I</dn> have been ridiculed all day long, everyone mocks me.
[8] For when <dn>I</dn> speak, <dn>I</dn> cry out, proclaiming violence and ruin. Because the word of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> was made to me a reproach and a derision daily.
[9] Whenever <dn>I</dn> said, “Let me not mention <dn>Him</dn>, nor speak in <dn>His</dn> Name again,” it was in <dn>my</dn> heart like a burning fire shut up in <dn>my</dn> bones. And <dn>I</dn> became weary of holding it back, and was helpless.
[10] For <dn>I</dn> heard many mocking, “Fear on every side!” “Expose,” they say, “yes, let us expose him!” All <dn>my</dn> friends watched for <dn>my</dn> stumbling, saying, “<dn>He</dn> might be lured away, so that we prevail against him, and take our revenge on him.”
[11] But <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with <dn>את</dn> me like a mighty, awesome one. Therefore <dn>my</dn> persecutors shall stumble, and not prevail. They shall be greatly ashamed, for they have not acted wisely – an everlasting reproach never to be forgotten.
[12] But, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> of hosts, trying the righteous, and seeing the kidneys and heart, let me see Your vengeance on them, for <dn>I</dn> have revealed <dn>my</dn> cause to You.
[13] Sing to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! Praise <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>! For <dn>He</dn> has delivered <dn>את</dn> the being of the poor from the hand of evil ones.

readings.title: Jeremiah's Lament
readings.subtitle: Cursing the Day of His Birth
readings.text:
[Jeremiah 20:14] Cursed be the day in which <dn>I</dn> was born! Let the day not be blessed in which <dn>my</dn> mother bore me!
[15] Let the man be cursed who brought news to <dn>my</dn> father, saying, “A male child has been born to you,” making him very glad.
[16] And let that man be like the cities which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> overthrew, and repented not. Let him hear the cry in the morning and the shouting at noon,
[17] because <dn>I</dn> was not slain from the womb, so that <dn>my</dn> mother should have been <dn>my</dn> burial-site and her womb forever great.
[18] Why did <dn>I</dn> come forth from the womb to see toil and sorrow, and spend <dn>my</dn> days in shame?

readings.title: The Siege of Jerusalem
readings.subtitle: Judah's King and Temple Vessels Taken
readings.text:
[Daniel 1:1] In the third year of the reign of Yehoyaqim, sovereign of Yehuḏah, Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar, sovereign of Baḇel came to Yerushalayim and besieged it.
[2] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave <dn>את</dn> Yehoyaqim sovereign of Yehuḏah into his hand, with some of the utensils of the House of <dn>Elohim</dn>, which he brought to the land of Shin‛ar to the house of his mighty one. And he brought <dn>את</dn> the utensils into the treasure house of his mighty one.

readings.title: The King's Decree
readings.subtitle: The Selection of the Hebrew Youths
readings.text:
[Daniel 1:3] And the sovereign said to Ashpenaz, the chief of his eunuchs, to bring some of the children of Yisra’ěl and some of the sovereign’s descendants and some of the nobles,
[4] young men in whom there was no blemish, but good-looking, having insight in all wisdom, having knowledge and understanding learning, capable to stand in the sovereign’s palace, and to teach them the writing and speech of the Kasdim.
[5] And the sovereign appointed for them a daily ration of the sovereign’s food and of the wine which he drank, and three years of training for them, so that at the end thereof they should stand before the sovereign.
[6] Now among them were from the sons of Yehuḏah: Dani’ěl, Ḥananyah, Misha’ěl, and Azaryah.
[7] And the chief of the eunuchs gave them names. For he called Dani’ěl, Bělteshatstsar; and Ḥananyah, Shaḏraḵ; and Misha’ěl, Měyshaḵ; and Azaryah, Aḇěḏ-Neḡo.

readings.title: A Test of Faith
readings.subtitle: Daniel's Resolve Not to Be Defiled
readings.text:
[Daniel 1:8] But Dani’ěl laid it upon his heart that he would not defile himself with the portion of the sovereign’s food, nor with the wine which he drank. So he asked permission from the chief of the eunuchs not to defile himself.
[9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> granted <dn>את</dn> Dani’ěl loving-commitment and compassion from the chief of the eunuchs,
[10] but the chief of the eunuchs said to Dani’ěl, “<dn>I</dn> fear <dn>my</dn> master the sovereign, who has appointed <dn>את</dn> your food and <dn>את</dn> your drink. For why should he see your faces looking worse than the young men who are your age? Then you would make <dn>את</dn> <dn>my</dn> head guilty before the sovereign!”
[11] And Dani’ěl said to the overseer whom the chief of the eunuchs had set over Dani’ěl, Ḥananyah, Misha’ěl, and Azaryah,
[12] “Please try your servants for ten days, and let them give us vegetables to eat and water to drink.
[13] “Then let our appearances be examined before you, and the appearances of the young men who eat the portion of the sovereign’s food. And do with your servants as you see fit.”
[14] And he listened to them in this matter, and tried them ten days.
[15] And at the end of ten days their appearances looked better and fatter in flesh than all the young men who ate the portion of the sovereign’s food.
[16] And it came to be that the overseer took away <dn>את</dn> their portion of food and the wine they were to drink, and gave them vegetables.

readings.title: Divine Favor and Wisdom
readings.subtitle: The Youths Excel Before Nebuchadnezzar
readings.text:
[Daniel 1:17] As for these four young men, <dn>Elohim</dn> gave them knowledge and skill in all learning and wisdom. And Dani’ěl had understanding in all visions and dreams.
[18] And at the end of the days, when the sovereign had said that they should be brought in, the chief of the eunuchs brought them in before Neḇuḵaḏnetstsar.
[19] And the sovereign spoke with them, and none among them all were found like Dani’ěl, Ḥananyah, Misha’ěl, and Azaryah, so they stood before the sovereign.
[20] And in any word of wisdom and understanding about which the sovereign examined them, he found them ten times better than all the magicians, the astrologers, who were in all his reign.
[21] And Dani’ěl continued until the first year of Sovereign Koresh.
